newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso hits 27-mth low on record volume.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso hits 27-mth low on record volume.

text.p: The Philippine peso recovered slightly at the close on Thursday after the Central Bank sold around $100 million to a foreign bank in late trade, dealers said.
The peso ended higher at 26.342 after falling to a 27-month-low of 26.345. But it was still lower than the previous day's close of 26.323.
"I have never seen anything like this," a trader said.

Volume hit a record $446.30 million, the highest since the market posted $383.6 million in August 23 last year after the peso fell on false rumours of the assassination of Defense Secretary Renato de Villa.
The peso had been weakening in the past three days due to a slide in domestic interest rates after Friday's cut in reserve requirements.
A trader said the Central Bank sold around $100 million to a foreign bank at $26.342 in late trades. Early in the day, the Central Bank sold less than $15 million.
Traders said offshore funds were probably moving out due to the narrower interest rate premium enjoyed by the peso over the U.S. dollar.
"I expect the Central Bank to increase its overnight rates by between 0.5 to 1.0 percentage-point on Friday to quell further speculation in the market," a trader said.
